caption: The drawing is done in pencil on a beige or off-white paper. It features a round bowl or shallow dish viewed from above, with a wide rim and a graduated circular depth indicated through shading. Attached to the top of the bowl is an ornate handle with symmetrical cut-out patterns and a stylized central motif resembling a fan or shell, decorated with scroll-like edges and a small, rounded cut-out at the top. The main circular object is centered inside a larger rectangular border drawn with a single line. Below the bowl, slightly right of center, is a smaller rectangular inset containing a technical side-view sketch of the bowl, labeled with measurements ("4 1/2", "3", and "2 1/2") and with arrows indicating the dimensions. The artist's signature, “Charles Cullen,” appears in cursive at the lower right corner just outside the main rectangle. The overall composition uses light and shadow for depth and is executed solely in pencil grays, with no applied color except the paper’s natural tone.
title: Silver Porringer
